scenarios.title: The Sacred Ridge Injunction
scenarios.clientName: Gram Sabha & Adivasi villagers of the Niyamgiri foothills
scenarios.bench: Two-Judge Bench of the Supreme Court of India (Constitution-civil)
scenarios.factualBackground: A state mining corporation holds a pending lease application for bauxite quarrying across a hill range that is sacred to the Dongria Kondh community. The district collector fast-tracked the lease without convening any gram sabha consultation, arguing tribal land records are incomplete and the 1994 lease is legally continuous.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether bauxite mining can proceed on recognised forest land inhabited by indigenous communities when no free, prior and informed gram sabha consent has been obtained under the FRA 2006, and whether the environmental clearance itself survives review.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Sri Arvind Thakre (Senior Advocate for the Corporation)
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, this is a strike of sentiment against sovereign need. The corporation holds a valid pre-FRA mineral concession, section 4(1) cannot be retrospectively applied, and the so-called 'sacred' claim is a manufactured barricade against industrial progress. I invite the Bench to note the staggering loss of revenue and employment the stay would occasion.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Jurisdiction and standing; whether the environmental clearance process already weighed tribal objections.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The Bench rises. It is your client's final opportunity to frame the injunction. Instruct the Court on what order preserves both the forest and the process.

scenarios.title: The Digital Blackout
scenarios.clientName: Civil society collectives and journalists based in a telecom circle
scenarios.bench: Constitution Bench proceedings on judicial review of the suspension
scenarios.factualBackground: Following a weekend of civic protests in a hill state, the Home Department issued an order suspending all internet and telecom services for an unspecified period, citing public order under the Telecom Suspension Rules. Access has now lapsed beyond three weeks; no notification of the order has been published, journalists cannot file copy, and digital payment systems remain down.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether a published, duration-unlimited telecom suspension survives challenge under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) read with Article 21, and what review machinery the Court must impose.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Mr. Rahul Bhattacharya (Senior Additional Advocate General)
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, sovereignty is not subordinate to social media. Section 69 of the IT Act and the Suspension Rules were exercised to prevent a wave of communal violence. The intermediateness of an inconvenience outweighed by the prevention of bloodshed. We shall show classified ground records that the situation remains live.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: State privilege over internal security records; proportionality in the abstract.

scenarios.closingPrompt: Time has come. Government persists. Give the Court the exact contours of the order it should pass on necessity, proportionality and transparency.

scenarios.title: The Midnight Eviction
scenarios.clientName: 1,242 families of the canal-belt 'unauthorised colony' under a flyover
scenarios.bench: Division Bench of a High Court hearing a town-planning PIL
scenarios.factualBackground: At 2:00 a.m., a demolition squad and police bulldozed the informal settlement lining an irrigation canal without any prior notice, confiscated two decades of domicile records, and dumped rubble over household goods. No rehabilitation offer has been made. The municipality claims the colony obstructs flood relief and cites an ex parte court order granted in its own writ.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether punitive nocturnal eviction of settled informal dwellings without notice, hearing or corrective action violates Article 21, and what restitution and relocation the Court should direct.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Smt. Meera Kompally (Standing Counsel for the Municipal Authority)
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, this is not an eviction but a statutory flood-control operation executed under a subsisting demolition order. These structures were built over the canal buffer in patent violation of building by-laws. The occupants had 20 years of constructive notice; a midnight execution harms nobody who obeyed the law.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Locus standi of the displaced; the finality of the municipal demolition order.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The rubble has been cleared from the galleries. Your final address will decide whether these families get restitution or a file number.

scenarios.title: The Platform Lockout
scenarios.clientName: A union of 500 platform delivery partners deactivated by a gig-app aggregator
scenarios.bench: Division Bench considering collective writ claims of gig workers
scenarios.factualBackground: Overnight, a food-delivery platform deactivated the accounts of 500 delivery partners in one city after a coordinated wage-strike, without any prior notice, hearing, or dispute-resolution forum. The commerce platform cites the terms-of-service 'independent contractor' clause and denies any employer relationship, while continuing to route orders through the same partners' replacements.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether mass deactivation of platform workers without hearing violates Articles 14, 19(1)(g) and 21, and whether the Code on Social Security 2020 and MV Aggregator Guidelines create enforceable entitlements notwithstanding the 'gig worker' label.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Mr. Vikram Nagarajan (Counsel for the Aggregator)
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, this is a private contract dispute dressed as a constitutional catastrophe. The partners accepted our terms, are free to run rival apps, and were deactivated for 'misconduct' under clause 12.4. They are merchants, not employees; the Code itself acknowledges the gig distinction. Collective writ petitions over private contracts are the wrong vehicle.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Justiciability of private labour contracts; the probative value of deactivation logs.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The Bench listens to the sound of emptied keyboards. Make the final case for why deactivation minus process can't bind these 500 workers.
